short: Mapping comparison (M06) and direct route (M08) standard for 2017; no silent test (M04) and no listener transcription (M12), both behind; label-free and paralinguistic claims unsupported.
position: The paper [@janke2017emg] changes two components, both standard for 2017. Its mapping comparison (M06) ranks four mappings over the field's usual time-domain EMG features, on 83 evaluation utterances and single runs (Appendix; Table I). Its output route (M08), direct mapping to MFCCs and F0 with an MLSA vocoder, was the route of 11 of 12 prior synthesis studies from non-acoustic signals (Appendix), so its case against recognition followed by synthesis targets a route prior work had barely used. Two incidental components are behind: no silent articulation is tested (M04), as six prior studies did, including the group's own first EMG-to-speech paper [@toth2009synthesizing], and intelligibility (M12) has no listener transcription, which five prior synthesis studies ran. The strongest overreach is the label-free claim, while the GMM and one LSTM use an LDA trained on audio-aligned phone sub-states (§III-A); retention of speaker identity and mood is asserted and not measured (§VI).
